summary: A dense Qwen3.8-27B (GPTQ INT4) served by vLLM 0.29.0 in tensor parallel 2 on one pair, under three arms: as built, with NCCL peer-to-peer disabled, and with both NCCL peer-to-peer and vLLM's custom all-reduce disabled, the software proxy for a pair without a bridge. Closing both paths cost about a tenth of single-stream speed and about a fifth of eight-request throughput; disabling NCCL peer-to-peer alone measured nothing, a false negative. The bridge was never physically removed, and each arm ran once.
title: Does the NVLink bridge matter? A dense 27B in tensor parallel 2
